column1: # 2026-10-31 (R5): user malloc under RLIMIT_AS: include/stdlib.h _unisa_map treats only -1 and 0 as failure, raw syscall 9 returns -ENOMEM (-12); the header ships inside the package, so the fix is a new candidate and changes every user image that links the allocator.

column1: # 2026-11-02 (R15): -S then -run on the same product SIGSEGVs; measured, not the tapebin wiring.

column3: the product cannot -run a tape that contains the .sys opcode: such a tape SIGSEGVs (rc 139), while a tape without it runs. Measured on the installed 0.0.43 and on candidate 2a40a7eb alike: any -S output for the current prelude carries at least two .sys lines (from the stdio write path) and dies on -run; the frozen 0.0.43 fixture tape decodes to 41 lines with no .sys and runs (rc 7). Tape size is not the variable - a one-line source already produces 12999 B, and truncating that tape makes -run refuse with rc 1 instead of dying. Pre-existing and unrelated to the TAPEBIN wiring 5216db7a13 (-b -o from the same tape writes an image that exits 7, and -run of the source itself works). The missing contract is the interpreter's .sys execution; a named refusal would also be acceptable. Note for whoever fixes it: the -run tape reader already refuses malformed tapes with rc 1, so a refusal path exists; .sys is recognised and then crashes rather than being refused, which suggests the cheap fix is to route it to that refusal
